Monsoon sustaining without outside help: Satellite spots India under rain spell
Satellite images show the monsoon sustaining itself with locally formed rain systems across India. The phase may bring short-term relief to rain-deficit northern states before a possible break next week.
ADVERTISEMENT
Satellite images captured on the evening of August 4 reveal widespread cloud cover. (Photo: Windy)
India Today Science Desk
New Delhi,UPDATED: Aug 5, 2026 07:00 IST
Subscribe to Notifications

India's southwest monsoon is currently running on its own momentum, with satellite imagery showing a vast swathe of the country under active rain-bearing systems that have developed entirely within the subcontinent, without any significant support from external weather disturbances.

Meteorologists say the monsoon is now being sustained by a series of "made in India" weather systems, a phase where local atmospheric conditions are driving rainfall instead of relying on moisture-laden depressions from the Bay of Bengal or other external influences.

Satellite images captured on the evening of August 4 reveal widespread cloud cover stretching across eastern and northern India as the monsoon trough deepens from West Bengal to Punjab.
